# Introduction

GeneTrackR connects annotation, genomic signal, variants, haplotypes and
phenotypes in a shared coordinate workflow. The intended use is to inspect a
candidate locus, construct genotype-defined groups, compare measured traits,
and retain the resulting tables and figures. Genomic plots provide context;
phenotype association alone does not establish a causal variant.

This is the first of six executable workflows. The examples use bundled
synthetic data and require no external data download. The package website is
<https://renscq.github.io/GeneTrackR/>.

## Position within Bioconductor

| Tool | Primary role | Relationship to this workflow |
|---|---|---|
| [Gviz](https://bioconductor.org/packages/Gviz/) | Track-oriented genomic visualization and annotation views | A mature option for genome-coordinate displays. GeneTrackR joins locus inspection to its haplotype and phenotype result objects. |
| [rtracklayer](https://bioconductor.org/packages/rtracklayer/) | Genomic file import/export and genome-browser infrastructure | Standard I/O infrastructure relevant to annotation and signal exchange. GeneTrackR currently retains its existing readers and writers. |
| [VariantAnnotation](https://bioconductor.org/packages/VariantAnnotation/) | Standard VCF/genotype representation and variant annotation | The appropriate infrastructure for typed VCF data and annotation tasks. GeneTrackR's VariantTrack currently stores point positions and raw sample fields for its analysis workflow. |
| GeneTrackR | Coordinated annotation/signal/variant visualization and haplotype-to-phenotype workflows | Provides connected analysis and plotting entry points, structured results and GRanges interchange. |

The comparison describes scope, not a performance ranking. GeneTrackR does not
implement all the capabilities of these packages. Its GRanges input/output is
implemented; a lossless VCF-class adapter and replacement I/O backends are future
work. The [class and I/O rationale](annotation.html#design-decisions) explains
the current boundaries and the evidence still needed for further reuse.

# Installation

GeneTrackR requires R >= 4.6.0 and is a Bioconductor submission candidate.
Until it is included in a release, development installation is:

```r
BiocManager::install(c("GenomicRanges", "IRanges", "S4Vectors"))
remotes::install_github("Renscq/GeneTrackR", dependencies = TRUE)
```

Install `BiocManager` and `remotes` first if they are not present. After
acceptance, use `BiocManager::install("GeneTrackR")` for the appropriate release.
`Rsamtools` is optional for indexed regional access. In-memory examples work
without it. `BiocStyle` is a suggested documentation dependency.

# Data model and designed truth {#demo-data}

All `gtr_demo_*` files describe one deterministic synthetic system. Values are
demonstration data, not measurements from biological samples.

| Input | Main contract |
|---|---|
| `gtr_demo.genePredExt`, `.gtf`, `.gff3` | Equivalent 20-gene, 24-transcript annotation |
| `gtr_demo_features.bed` | Fifteen interval annotations around the designed loci |
| `gtr_demo_*plus.bedgraph`, `gtr_demo_*minus.bedgraph` | Strand-specific RNA-seq/Ribo-seq signals |
| `gtr_demo_variants.vcf` | 56 variants and 36 samples, with FORMAT/sample fields |
| `gtr_demo_pheno.tsv` | Numeric and categorical traits keyed by `sample_id` |
| `scripts/demo_model/truth.tsv` | Packaged source table for selected designed effects |

GeneA has four genotype-defined haplotypes with nine samples each. Its synthetic
traits contain designed positive controls; `flowering_time` is a negative
control with the same group distributions. The LD example contains twelve
variants with a perfect six-variant core and weaker downstream relationships.
These controls demonstrate expected behavior and do not validate a biological
mechanism.

```{r inputs}
gp <- read_genepred(demo_file("gtr_demo.genePredExt"), format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
vcf <- read_vcf(demo_file("gtr_demo_variants.vcf"), mode = "memory",
  verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
pheno <- read_pheno(demo_file("gtr_demo_pheno.tsv"), verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(gp$genes) == 20L, nrow(gp$transcripts) == 24L,
  nrow(vcf$data) == 56L, length(vcf$meta$sample_names) == 36L, nrow(pheno) == 36L)
head(list.files(system.file("extdata", package = "GeneTrackR"), pattern = "^gtr_demo_"))
```

## Coordinates and sample identifiers

Internal intervals are **1-based closed**. BED/bedGraph file coordinates are
converted at the file boundary. VCF records are stored as 1-based point
positions, including indels. Check genome assembly, chromosome names, strand,
units and sample identifiers before combining real inputs.

The phenotype rows deliberately differ from VCF sample order. Matching uses
`sample_id`, never row position. Report both input sizes and losses before
joining data:

```{r sample-alignment}
vcf_ids <- vcf$meta$sample_names
pheno_ids <- as.character(pheno$sample_id)
shared_ids <- intersect(vcf_ids, pheno_ids)
data.frame(vcf_samples = length(vcf_ids), phenotype_samples = length(pheno_ids),
  shared = length(shared_ids), vcf_only = length(setdiff(vcf_ids, pheno_ids)),
  phenotype_only = length(setdiff(pheno_ids, vcf_ids)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(vcf_ids), !anyDuplicated(pheno_ids),
  length(shared_ids) == 36L, !identical(vcf_ids, pheno_ids))
```

# First locus and haplotypes

```{r first-gene}
genea <- retrieve_feature(gp, gene_id = "GeneA")
genea$genes
plot_gene(gp, gene_id = "GeneA", text_size = 10) & classic_style
```

```{r first-haplotypes}
hap <- hap_gene_variant(vcf, annotation = gp, gene_id = "GeneA", genotype_mode = "string")
hap$haplotypes
stopifnot(nrow(hap$haplotypes) == 4L, all(hap$haplotypes$sample_n == 9L))
```

Genotype encoding, missing calls, phasing and grouping choices should be made
explicit for real data. The [variant and haplotype workflow](haplotype.html)
explains those decisions before association testing.

# Entry points and returned objects

| Task | Recommended entry | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Read annotation | `read_genepred()`, `read_gtf()`, `read_gff()`, `read_bed()` | Feature-compatible annotation |
| Construct intervals | `Feature()` or `as_feature(gr)` | Feature, also inheriting FeatureTrack |
| Read signals | `read_bwg()` | BwgTrack with sample/mode metadata |
| Read variants | `read_vcf()` | VariantTrack |
| Construct haplotypes | `hap_gene_variant()`, `hap_region_variant()` | HapVariant |
| Compare numeric traits | `plot_hap_pheno()`, `plot_variant_pheno()` | Tables and `$figure` |
| Compute/plot LD | `compute_ld_block()`, `plot_ld_block()` | LDTrack; plot stored in `$figure` |

`FeatureTrack()` and `read_vcf_track()` remain supported aliases of `Feature()`
and `read_vcf()`. Existing names, argument defaults and return objects remain
supported. Plotting functions that return a result object require `$figure`
when a ggplot/patchwork is needed for saving or composition.
